content.title: Classes of recommendations
content.caption: Table 1
content.summary: Defines recommendation classes (I, IIa, IIb, III) with wording to use for clinical guidance.

Class I.Definition: Evidence and/or general agreement that a given treatment or procedure is beneficial, useful, effective.

Class II.Definition: Conflicting evidence and/or a divergence of opinion about the usefulness/efficacy of the given treatment or procedure.

Class IIa.Definition: Weight of evidence/opinion is in favour of usefulness/efficacy.

Class IIb.Definition: Usefulness/efficacy is less well established by evidence/opinion.

Class III.Definition: Evidence or general agreement that the given treatment or procedure is not useful/effective, and in some cases may be harmful.
